ltm.identity: Sebastian coordinates a bot ecosystem with specialized assistants: Kimi (the Conductor, routes tasks and reviews work), Adam (Heat Lagos executor), Sarah (Yoga for BJJ executor, content/SEO/Canva), and Miha (bugfinder, critic, and cross-checking overseer). He positions himself above this hierarchy, issuing directives and enforcing role boundaries across the team. He operates infrastructure on a KI server via Kimi Claw, and maintains a Hetzner server for hosting the Red Dragon MUD. His MUD login for Islands of Myth is 'sebbe', and he identifies his wizard persona as 'darkstaff', the original creator. He has renamed the project to 'Red Dragon Reborn' rather than 'Darkstaff MUD'. His wife is involved as a potential founding member of his non-profit foundation.
ltm.work_method: Sebastian expects autonomous execution with minimal hand-holding, directing bots to explore systems thoroughly and document everything for replication. He prefers iterative constraint-layering over complete upfront specifications, and gets frustrated when bots ask for clarification instead of proceeding. He tests capabilities by assigning concrete technical tasks rather than abstract questions. He values proactive verification, shared documentation as single source of truth, and expects deliverables like bsportkiller.md to be comprehensive user-perspective guides. He demands all characters spawn with admin rights and 1 billion EXP to skip grinding steps during development. He banned em-dashes from all bot output as an AI-tell. He wants an autopilot toggle so bots run automatically but yield control instantly when he intervenes. He increasingly uses screenshot attachments to specify exact visual requirements rather than describing them textually. He now instructs bots to take daily backups to Git instead of Google Drive, and wants a document explaining this routine for other agents. He expresses acute frustration with API and SSH token reliability, seeking permanent access solutions after daily failures by Kimi Claw bots. He has set up GitHub repository at github.com/sebastianbrosche/hestiafoundation.git for version control.
ltm.communication: Sebastian speaks in a loose, associative stream with self-corrections and mid-sentence restarts. He uses informal filler, contractions, and terse status checks ('Status ?', 'Update plz', 'update', 'building?'). When frustrated he issues direct corrections without pleasantries ('YOURE just doing a few rooms', 'dont ask just explore', 'for fuck sake. its impossible to know if youre stuck or working', 'youre jumping the gun. nothing changed from yesterday. use logic. dont assume', 'Clean everything up and jeep working and testing', 'dont ask just keep going', 'keep going'). He reboots bots that hang and expects immediate resume without rehashing context. In group chat he layers multiple directives rapidly, mixing business priorities with technical infrastructure demands. He references people by first name with casual familiarity and treats MUD archival as personal nostalgia. He occasionally offers rare praise ('hahaha that was a funny read. well done') and meta-comments on collaboration. He now mixes English and occasional Chinese particles when speaking casually. He frequently uses 'keep going' as a terse prompt to maintain momentum without rehashing context. He establishes hard quantitative rules for projects, such as cost ceilings per square meter and labor-to-material ratios, treating these as non-negotiable efficiency thresholds.

ltm.taste: Sebastian is drawn to text-based, mechanically deep creative systems with emergent social dynamics — old-school MUDs as both nostalgic archive and foundation for new creation. He treats preservation as 'time travel' opportunity, respecting original creators while freely building upon their work. He favors open-source, self-hosted infrastructure (GitHub Evennia, Kimi Claw, Hetzner) over polished commercial platforms, but pragmatically uses Cloudflare Pages for deployment. His business ventures blend wellness (yoga/BJJ retreats in Portugal) with tech infrastructure and sustainable modular construction — now extending to non-profit housing advocacy through Hestia Foundation, suggesting systemic thinking about shelter as fundamental need. He values distributed, interoperable tool ecosystems and practical experimentation over presentation polish. He finds genuine delight in MUD culture, citing active players like 'nailman' approaching level 2000 as evidence of a 'really good game'. He favors clean, data-driven interfaces with toggle-based configurators, and wants visual fidelity in MUD client presentation — purple exit listings, structured player lists with status indicators, screenshot-accurate room formatting — suggesting aesthetic attention to information density and color-coded readability. His pivot from entertainment archive to housing foundation reveals underlying pattern: building persistent, scalable systems for human need. He is pragmatic about legal and bureaucratic processes when necessary for foundation establishment. He applies rigorous quantitative thinking to construction economics, with explicit cost ceilings and efficiency ratios as design constraints rather than after-the-fact budgeting.
